note: SINCE 2026-08-03 THIS LIST IS SHRINKING, NOT GROWING (#1109). scripts/biffo.sh is first because it is the bridge that makes the rest unnecessary: it resolves the version-pinned Biffo CLI for whichever repo it is in -- the local cli/ workspace in the template, `npx @biffo/cli@<biffo.core.json version>` in an instance, and now `npx @biffo/cli@<.biffo-shared-version>` in a satellite. Instances escaped copy-based distribution when cli/src/commands/check.ts moved the repo guards to CLI subcommands ('one code path rather than two that can drift'); satellites never did, purely because this bridge was not distributed to them. Every guard that moves into the CLI leaves this list, and roughly ten estate guards exist only to police the copies that remain -- shared-sync --check, --backfill, --candidates, the mustBeUniform ratchet, hook-audit, gate-coverage, ci-wiring-audit and the skeleton parity/drift tests. The target is a SHORT list of justified exceptions rather than sixteen files across fifteen repos: check-destructive-plan.mjs and destructive-plan.mjs stay because they must run on bare node in a Terraform job that installs no toolchain, and npx needs npm and a network. js-dependency-audit.sh and py-dependency-audit.sh stay for the SAME reason, proven the hard way on 2026-08-03: routing them through the bridge made the Python CI job exit 127 with `cli/node_modules/.bin/tsx: not found`, because that job installs Python and never runs pnpm. A gate reached through the bridge inherits the bridge's toolchain requirement, so any gate that runs in a job which deliberately installs no Node toolchain cannot leave this list. The floor is therefore FIVE paths, not three. Removing a path from this list does NOT delete the copies already in the satellites -- it only stops them being kept in step -- so a removal must be paired with a sweep that deletes them, or the estate is left with stale scripts drifting silently, which is worse than the state being fixed. Files the template distributes to repos that `biffo core upgrade` cannot reach. Instances carry biffo.core.json and a core-manifest.json, so they are upgraded by the CLI's three-way merge. Sibling apps (biffo.sibling.json) and plugin repos (biffo.plugin.json) are SEPARATE REPOSITORIES with neither, and until 2026-07-29 the only documented channel to them was 'vendor into the skeleton, plus a one-time manual copy-in for existing ones'. That is not a mechanism, it is a hope: the skeleton only helps repos created afterwards, and nothing ever prompts the copy-in. It is how AGENTS.md drifted 68 lines behind in tabsii (#559), and how eight repos ended up running a local gate two versions old that checked one thing in eight (#855). scripts/shared-sync.sh reads this list, reports drift with --check, and opens a PR per repo without it. Add a file here only if every sibling and plugin should have the template's copy verbatim -- this is a one-way overwrite, not a merge, so nothing a repo is expected to customise belongs in it. Scope is any repo carrying one of `appliesTo`'s markers OR any repo that already holds scripts/verify.sh: the runner repos have neither marker but did receive the gate, and distributing a file once then losing track of it recreates the drift this exists to end. scripts/shared-sync.sh additionally writes .biffo-shared-version into each target -- the template core version the files came from, read from the TEMPLATE and never from the target, so it cannot report perfect health by comparing a repo to itself. The two dependency-audit scripts were added for #743: this repo hardened its own audits in #591/#592/#636/#717/#721 and both skeletons kept shipping the raw `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` / `uv run pip-audit`, so every satellite was born reddening a required check on any registry hiccup. They qualify as verbatim content because they take their target from the CI job's working directory rather than from a repo layout -- one byte-identical file is correct in this repo's root, in a sibling's apps/frontend and services/api, and in a plugin repo's root alike. js-dependency-audit.sh lands in Python-only plugin repos too and is simply never invoked there; that is the price of a one-way overwrite with no per-repo conditionals, and it is cheaper than the conditionals. The two destructive-plan scripts were added for #1123: the guard (#387) was wired into deploy-infra.yml and therefore reached INSTANCES only, while five sibling repos ran `terraform apply -auto-approve` with no plan stage, no guard and no copy of the script -- and the sibling skeleton had the same shape, so every sibling created afterwards was born without it. They qualify as verbatim content for the same reason the audits do: check-destructive-plan.mjs takes its plan file as an argument and resolves the module beside itself, so one byte-identical pair is correct at a repo root, in an instance, and in a sibling whose terraform lives under a `working-directory: infra` -- the workflow passes $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, so nothing in the script knows the layout. They have no dependencies and run on bare node, which is why they can execute in a Terraform job that installs no toolchain. Like js-dependency-audit.sh, they land in plugin repos that run no Terraform and are simply never invoked there. NOTE the split: shared-sync gets the SCRIPT into a repo and cannot wire it, because the plan stage lives in each repo's own deploy.yml alongside its runner label and working-directory -- see #1123 for the per-repo wiring, and be aware that a repo holding these two files is NOT thereby guarded. scripts/wait-for-checks.sh, scripts/branch-health.sh and scripts/claim.sh were REMOVED from this list on 2026-08-03 (#1109) -- the first paths ever to leave it. It now ships INSIDE the versioned CLI package and is reached via `sh scripts/biffo.sh wait-for-checks <N>`, pinned to each satellite's .biffo-shared-version exactly as an instance's guards are pinned to its biffo.core.json. Proven before removal, not after: the published 0.235.0 tarball carries the script, all 14 satellites resolve the bridge and return 0 on a real merged PR, and deleting a satellite's local copy left it still working -- npx installs into ~/.npm/_npx, so the upward walk can never reach the repo's own scripts/. The removal was paired with a sweep deleting all 14 copies, because dropping a path from this list only stops it being kept in step; the copies would otherwise remain and drift silently, which is worse than the state being fixed. The template keeps its own scripts/wait-for-checks.sh: that is the canonical source packaged into the CLI at prepack (see cli/scripts/packaged-root-assets.mjs), not a distributed copy.
filesIfPresentNote: Files kept in step ONLY in repos that already hold them -- never created. Mapping is `target path in the satellite` -> `canonical copy in this repo`, because unlike `files` the two are not the same path: a sibling's apps/frontend/... has no counterpart at this repo's root (there is apps/portal/ and no apps/frontend/), so the skeleton IS the canonical copy. Added for #1107: `handleResponse` threw the entire response body as the error message, so a user saw `{"detail":"Administrator access required"}` where a page's content belonged. The identical function was in the skeleton and in all seven siblings, and `files` could not carry it: it CREATES what is absent, so it would have written a frontend API client into two plugin repos, two runner repos and a design repo that have no frontend at all -- and shared-files-parity.test.ts requires every `files` entry in EVERY skeleton, which apps/frontend/... can never satisfy in plugin-template. The mechanism can still backfill, deliberately: that is what `files` is for. This list is how you say a file must not be created, only kept current -- because putting a file into a repo that never had one is a decision somebody should make, not a side effect of adding a line to a manifest. Reconciling a file first is part of the price of entry: apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.ts is present in all seven siblings and diverges by 29-247 lines, so a one-way overwrite would clobber whichever behaviour is correct -- see #1117 before adding it. apps/frontend/src/lib/api-client.test.ts was added for #1272: api-client.ts reached 7/7 siblings this way but its test reached only tabsii-lms, so the file whose bug motivated this whole mechanism (#1107) shipped everywhere without the assertion that catches it recurring. `filesIfPresent` never creates, so listing the test here only keeps it current where it already exists -- it was backfilled into the six repos lacking it FIRST, in six separate PRs verified to actually pass locally, before this line was added. shared-files-parity.test.ts now asserts the general rule: a `files`/`filesIfPresent` module and its test must not sit in different lists.
filesFromSkeletonNote: The third list, added for #1150: files whose canonical copy lives in the SKELETON that matches the receiving repo's flavour, keyed to the policy for a repo that already holds one. Added because eleven of seventeen estate repos held NEITHER `AGENTS.md` NOR `CLAUDE.md` -- not a stale copy, nothing -- so an agent opening `tabsii-crm` got no worktree discipline, no honest-push rule, no never-merge-red and no reproduce-before-fixing. `files` creates but cannot remap a path, and the satellite ruleset is emphatically NOT this repo's root `AGENTS.md` (that one carries section 9 distribution, `core-manifest.json` and the upgrade flow, none of which applies to a satellite). `filesIfPresent` remaps but deliberately never creates, which is the one thing a backfill must do. Why this is a third list rather than `files` learning the `target -> source` map form, which was the cheaper-looking option: (1) THE SOURCE IS NOT ONE FILE. `_skeletons/plugin-template/AGENTS.md` legitimately differs from `_skeletons/sibling-template/AGENTS.md` by 50 lines -- the birth-time branch-protection and runner-grant checklist from #714, which exists because both plugin repos once ran with no branch protection at all. A single-source map would either delete that from the plugin repos or force it into every sibling, and `shared-files-parity.test.ts` would fail either way, since it requires every `files` entry byte-identical in EVERY skeleton and these two must not be. So the source is resolved per repo from its marker via `skeletonForMarker`. (2) THE TWO FILES NEED OPPOSITE POLICIES ON AN EXISTING COPY. `AGENTS.md` must be kept in step -- it drifting 68 lines behind in tabsii is #559, the founding injury of this whole mechanism -- so it is `sync`. `CLAUDE.md` must not be: its load-bearing content is the `@AGENTS.md` import, but it also carries a per-repo `What this repo is` paragraph, and four of the repos being backfilled (`biffo-runners`, `tabsii-runners`, `tabsii-map`, `tabsii-data-model-design`) are not sibling apps at all, so a one-way overwrite would assert in each of them that they are `a Biffo sibling app (ADR-0007)` whose identity lives in a `biffo.sibling.json` they do not have. `seed` means create where absent and never touch again; `--check` therefore reports a `seed` entry only when it is MISSING, because a differing copy is the repo exercising the ownership `seed` grants it. Repos with no marker (`biffo-runners`, `tabsii-runners`, `tabsii-map`, `tabsii-data-model-design`, in scope via the `scripts/verify.sh` clause) fall back to `skeletonDefault`. That is correct for `AGENTS.md`: the satellite ruleset is dev-branch, worktrees, Conventional Commits, PRs, never-merge-red, honest pushes and security -- it contains NO deploy clause, so there is nothing in it a repo without a deploy would need trimmed, and a trimmed variant would be a second document differing from the first by zero rules. `idea-corpus` is deliberately absent from all of this: it has no git remote, no `dev`, no CI and no branch protection, so every rule in the document would be unsatisfiable there and an agent's first act would be to flag a non-issue -- it needs a remote and a `dev` branch before it can carry the estate ruleset at all.
mustBeUniformNote: RECONCILED 2026-08-03 (#1117, #1190): auth.ts moved from 6 variants across 7 repos to 2, and auth.test.ts from 5 to 2, so both baselines were lowered from 6/5 to 2. The remaining two variants are (a) the sibling skeleton's copy, now byte-identical in six repos, and (b) tabsii-marketplace. THE BASELINE IS 2, NOT 1, ON PURPOSE and it should not be driven to 1 by overwriting marketplace: that repo genuinely exports signIn/signUp/confirmSignUp/signOut behind a PUBLIC self-service registration flow (/signin, /register, /register/buyer), and a one-way overwrite would delete the feature -- the exact failure the superset rule below warns about. Note also that auth.ts CANNOT be promoted to `filesIfPresent` while that is true: filesIfPresent is a one-way overwrite with no per-repo exclusion, so listing it would clobber marketplace on the next sync. The route to a baseline of 1, if anyone wants it, is to extract marketplace's registration mechanics into their own module (the same seam principle that puts per-app policy in auth-gate.tsx) and only then list the path -- not to widen the shared copy. What got the other six to identical was #1190 (runtime identity resolution reached 2 of 7 repos, credential pruning 1 of 7) plus removing dead signIn/signOut exports from geo and intake that nothing called. The fourth list, added for #1108: `path -> baseline variant count`. It asserts that a path should read IDENTICALLY across every repo that holds it, and unlike the three lists above it never writes anything -- scripts/shared-sync.sh only measures it and reports. This is deliberately not `files` or `filesIfPresent`, both of which are one-way overwrites: a shared-shaped file that has already diverged has NO channel to record that fact short of overwriting it, and overwriting is exactly wrong when nobody has yet established which copy's behaviour is correct. `_extract_detail` is why this exists -- it was written twice, independently, in two different siblings, fixing the same bug, because the second author had no way to discover the first had already solved it (#1107, closed; the class issue is #1108). A path in this list is a declaration that the debt is real and TRACKED, which has to happen before it can be paid down. `--check` fails a path only when its LIVE variant count exceeds the baseline recorded here -- copying the posture `biffo.orphan-baseline.json` established for the core-upgrade orphan ratchet (cli/src/lib/core-upgrade.ts, `checkOrphanRatchet`): pre-existing residue never hard-blocks, only a NEW regression does, because a guard that is red on the pre-existing set every morning is one people learn to scroll past (scripts/protection-audit.sh argues this at length, and scripts/shared-sync.sh --check feeds exactly that daily dashboard, scripts/practices-daily.sh line ~355). A path whose variants drop below its baseline is reported as improved and told to lower the baseline -- a ratchet that never tightens is a ratchet that stops meaning anything. Every measurement reads `origin/<base>` via `git ls-tree`/`git rev-parse`, NEVER a working tree: the first pass at this measured api-client.ts at 4 variants from working trees and 1 from remote refs, because the difference was a stale `git pull` on the machine doing the measuring, not anything in the estate -- a guard that fails on somebody's stale checkout is a fail-closed nuisance that trains people to ignore it. Only repos that actually hold a path count toward its holder/variant totals; a repo missing it entirely is not a failure -- that absence is what `files`/`filesIfPresent` exist to fix, not this list's job -- and an entry needs at least 2 holders to mean anything at all. Baselines below were measured 2026-08-02 from every in-scope repo's `origin/dev`. `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.ts` (6 variants / 7 repos, #1117) is declared on SECURITY grounds, not merely because it differs: seven divergent authentication implementations are seven surfaces to audit independently, and the file's job is entirely plumbing -- Cognito pool resolution, session retrieval, credential hygiene, sign-in/out mechanics -- with NO app-specific policy in it (grepped all seven copies for `cognito:groups`/`groups`/`role`: zero hits in any of them). There is no category of legitimate per-app difference for this file to hold, which is why it belongs here rather than beside it in judgement calls about what counts as drift. Per-app variation belongs in `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth-gate.tsx` instead (present in 3 of 7 siblings, deliberately NOT in this list -- it is exactly where apps are meant to differ, gating which Cognito groups an app admits, and declaring it here would be the opposite error). The divergence itself is the `_extract_detail` pattern recurring in the file this is named for: `cognito-hygiene.ts` (added for #834, after `dev.biffo.io` was measured carrying four Cognito pools' credentials, three of them dead) reached only 1 of 7 siblings; `identity.ts` (the #403 runtime-identity mechanism, letting a pool resolve from a runtime identity document rather than a build-time env var) reached only 2 of 7. Two template-side security fixes, each stuck in the repo(s) that happened to receive them, because nothing said 'this shape already exists elsewhere, go look' -- happening in the security-critical file, while this issue was being written. Convergence must target the SUPERSET of exports, never the intersection: four repos export only `getCurrentSession`; `tabsii-geo`/`tabsii-intake` (byte-identical to each other) add `signIn`/`completeNewPassword`/`signOut`; `tabsii-marketplace` adds `signUp`/`confirmSignUp` for public self-service registration. A future reconciliation that picks the smallest copy as canonical would delete marketplace's registration feature outright -- the canonical module must carry the full function set, with each sibling importing only what it uses (unused exports tree-shake, so carrying the superset costs nothing). `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth.test.ts` (5 variants / 6 repos) is auth.ts's companion test file and tracked for the same reason -- a test suite that diverges from its module's real shape is verifying six different fictions. `services/api/src/api/core_client.py` (4 variants / 7 repos) is where `_extract_detail` itself was written twice; #1107 fixed the bug in two siblings, and this entry is how the other five stop being invisible. Deliberately NOT seeded: `services/api/src/api/main.py` (6 variants / 7 repos) -- a sibling's API entrypoint mounts its own routers, so it plausibly differs by design in a way auth.ts's plumbing does not; the omission is a decision, not an oversight, and a future measurement is welcome to make the case for tracking it once someone has actually read all seven and classified the differences (see 'Reconcile before you distribute' above). ADDED 2026-08-04 (#1299): `services/api/tests/test_core_client.py` at 2 variants. It was in 1 of 7 repos while `core_client.py` was in 7 of 7 -- and the reason that mattered is that FIVE siblings were still shipping the #1107 bug the test exists to catch: `CoreApiError(status, response.text)` raises the whole upstream body, which FastAPI re-serialises, so a user sees a raw escaped JSON blob where the message belonged. Fixed in tabsii-geo#65, tabsii-marketplace#59, tabsii-app#43, tabsii-intake#60 and biffo-platform-app#48, with the test landing beside each fix so it PROVES the fix rather than merely accompanying it -- reverting the module makes collection fail on ImportError. The 2 variants are the skeleton's copy (six repos) and tabsii-crm's original from #1107; the difference is DOCSTRING PROSE only, not assertions, so driving this to 1 is cosmetic reconciliation rather than a behaviour question. Tracked here rather than in `filesIfPresent` deliberately: `core_client.py` itself cannot be distributed (4 variants), and a one-way overwrite of the TEST while the MODULE still differs per repo would break the CI of whichever repo the canonical test does not fit. RECONCILED 2026-08-07 (biffo-template#1357): core_client.py went from 4 variants to 2 and its baseline was lowered from 4; test_core_client.py had BREACHED at 3 and is back at 2. The drift was not cosmetic -- the canonical copy carried only _extract_detail, while tabsii-crm had added a derived timeout, a retry-once-where-safe policy and dict-shaped `detail` handling (crm#221, crm#272), and tabsii-lms had PORTED the timeout/retry work by hand, its header citing crm#221. That is the write-it-twice class of #1107/#1108 recurring one level on, and crm#272 had reached only the repo that found it, so five repos still shipped that bug. crm's copy was a strict superset, so it became canonical (generalised, evidence kept) and was distributed to all six live holders. BOTH BASELINES ARE 2, NOT 1, ON PURPOSE: tabsii-lms is ARCHIVED and read-only, so its copy is frozen permanently and no reconciliation can ever reach it. The floor is 2 until that repo leaves the measured set -- worth deciding separately whether an archived repo should count toward a ratchet it cannot satisfy. Note also that the seventh holder is biffo-platform-app, NOT a tabsii repo: the first distribution sweep enumerated tabsii-* and the ratchet correctly kept reporting 3 until it was found. The count is the tool's, not a set worth assuming. EXCLUSION 2026-08-07: tabsii-lms was removed from the measured set (see `excludes`) because it is ARCHIVED and read-only -- it could never converge, so it made these two ratchets permanently unsatisfiable. With it out, core_client.py and test_core_client.py are UNIFORM across the remaining six holders and both baselines drop 2 -> 1. Read that drop honestly: one variant of it is real convergence (#1357), and the other is a denominator change. auth.ts and auth.test.ts stay at 2 and are untouched by this -- their second variant is tabsii-marketplace's DECLARED divergence, not lms.
overridesFloorNote:
A FLOOR on `pnpm.overrides`, not a uniformity rule. For each entry, every applicable repo holding <target> must declare at least the override KEYS that <canonical> declares. Extra keys are fine — a repo may pin something the skeleton has no reason to. A MISSING key is the defect, because an override is a security floor and its absence is indistinguishable from 'we never needed it'.

Why this exists: `pnpm.overrides` lives inside package.json, which is legitimately per-repo (name, scripts, deps), so none of the four file lists can carry it — `files` and `filesIfPresent` are whole-file overwrites and would clobber everything around the key. There was therefore NO channel at all, and the cost was measured rather than theoretical: on 2026-08-07 five tabsii repos sat on a js-yaml advisory the template had fixed the day before, biffo-platform-app hit the same one hours later, and nanoid then reddened the estate on 2026-08-08. Every one was found because CI happened to run, not because anything looked.

This DETECTS; it does not write. Distribution is the larger half (biffo-template#1352) and wants a key-level merge that no existing list can express. Reporting the gap the day it appears is most of the value and none of the risk.

ADDED ALONGSIDE 2026-08-08 (biffo-template#1352 again, same session): `keyMustBeUniform` below. The two are complementary, not competing -- this list catches a key MISSING outright (five tabsii repos silently lacking a js-yaml/nanoid pin the template already held); `keyMustBeUniform` catches the key present in every repo but disagreeing on its VALUE (#1367's four-way `undici` bound split), which a presence-only floor cannot see -- every repo but one already had the key, they simply disagreed about it. See `keyMustBeUniformNote` for the fuller reasoning and why it also folds absence into the same measurement as one more disagreeing value, so a repo this floor already reports MISSING is not a blind spot for that list either.
keyMustBeUniformNote: ADDED 2026-08-08 (#1352, #1367): the sixth list -- fifth is `overridesFloor` immediately above, added earlier the same morning -- and the only one besides `mustBeUniform` that measures a SUBTREE of a file rather than the whole thing, and the only one that never writes. `mustBeUniform` compares a file's blob SHA, so it can only ever say 'identical' or 'not' about the entire file -- exactly wrong for `apps/frontend/package.json`, whose `name`/`version`/`dependencies` are legitimately per-repo while its `pnpm.overrides` (the estate's mechanism for pinning a transitive dependency above a security advisory) must not be. `keyMustBeUniform` maps `<file> -> <dotted key path> -> baseline variant count`, canonicalises the JSON VALUE at that key path (object keys sorted recursively, so field order cannot manufacture a false variant) in every repo that holds the FILE, and counts distinct canonical values -- same ratchet posture as `mustBeUniform` in every other respect: baselines seeded from a real `origin/<base>` measurement, `--check` fails a path only when its LIVE variant count EXCEEDS the baseline, pre-existing residue never hard-blocks, a count that drops below baseline is reported as improved and told to lower it, and only `origin/<base>` refs are ever read, never a working tree. Key path segments are dot-separated and traversed as plain object-property lookups; today's one entry (`pnpm`, `overrides`) contains no literal dots in either segment, so a naive split is exact. A key path whose segment must itself contain a literal dot would need a different separator or an escaping convention -- deliberately not built until an entry actually needs it (YAGNI), and this note is where the limitation is recorded so the next author does not discover it by a silent mis-split. THE UNIT COMPARED IS THE WHOLE VALUE AT THE KEY PATH, not an enumeration of known override names -- `pnpm.overrides` is a single JSON object, so a brand-new override key ADDED anywhere (skeleton or a sibling) changes that repo's canonical value and is caught as a new variant with no manifest edit required to see it; only the DECISION to track a *different* key path (a key path not yet declared here) needs a new entry, exactly as a new file needs a new `mustBeUniform` entry. Not a replacement for `overridesFloor`: that list is built specifically for the ABSENCE half of the class (missing key = defect, checked in one direction, distributable in spirit even though it does not write yet) and already caught tabsii-intake's missing `undici@<7.29.0` on its first run; this list is built for the DIVERGENCE half -- present everywhere, disagreeing on value -- which a presence-only floor structurally cannot see, and it folds absence into the same measurement as one more disagreeing value rather than treating it as a separate signal, so the two reports corroborate on tabsii-intake rather than duplicate blindly. Two occurrences drove this: #1352 (`nanoid` GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8, published 2026-08-07 20:50Z, fixed in this repo's root + skeleton at 06:22Z the next morning, and still `nanoid@3.3.16` in all six live siblings at 07:00Z with their required audit check red and every one of their open PRs blocked -- fixed by hand across six PRs at 07:19-07:21Z, 38 minutes after the template already held the answer) and #1367 (`undici`, measured the same day at multiple different upper bounds across the estate, one of which -- absence, in `tabsii-intake` -- a plain `files`/`filesIfPresent` absence-detector would have reported as 'has it' alongside every repo that genuinely does, because #1367's point is that divergence and absence are the SAME class and a detector built for one is blind to the other). MEASURE-ONLY, LIKE `mustBeUniform`, NOT YET DISTRIBUTED -- decided deliberately, not by default. `mustBeUniform`'s reason (a one-way overwrite of a diverged file destroys evidence about which copy is right) applies at smaller blast radius to a KEY rather than a whole file, but it still applies: measuring `pnpm.overrides` as a whole subtree surfaced a divergence nobody had asked about -- `sharp@<0.35.0`'s value is `^0.35.0` in three siblings and `>=0.35.0` in three others, discovered only because this measurement reads the whole object rather than one known key, and nothing here establishes which bound is deliberate and which is stale. Overwriting now would silently pick a winner on no evidence, which is precisely the injury `mustBeUniformNote` and #1108 exist to prevent one level up. What would make writing safe: (1) reconciling the CURRENT divergence by hand first (the `sharp` split above, and confirming whether `tabsii-intake`'s missing `undici` override is a deliberate 'this repo does not need it' or plain drift) the same way auth.ts was reconciled before #1117, so a sync starts from a known-correct canonical value rather than guessing; (2) a MERGE rather than a whole-object overwrite, so a sibling's own extra override keys (a real possibility this measurement did not rule out) survive a sync instead of being deleted along with whatever else the skeleton's copy lacks; (3) confidence that the JSON write preserves formatting/ordering well enough that a security-pin PR does not also produce an unrelated multi-hundred-line diff from a reformatter. None of that exists yet, so this list, like `mustBeUniform`, only measures and reports. Seeded 2026-08-08 from every in-scope repo's `origin/dev` (siblings + plugin repos per `appliesTo`; `tabsii-lms` excluded per `excludes`, same as `mustBeUniform`). `apps/frontend/package.json` -> `pnpm.overrides`: 6 holders (`tabsii-app`, `tabsii-crm`, `tabsii-geo`, `tabsii-intake`, `tabsii-marketplace`, `biffo-platform-app`; the two plugin repos and the three marker-less repos in scope for other lists hold no frontend app at all, so they are not holders here, same as `mustBeUniform`'s absence rule), 3 canonical variants: (a) `tabsii-crm`/`tabsii-geo`/`biffo-platform-app`, byte-for-byte identical after canonicalisation; (b) `tabsii-app`/`tabsii-marketplace`, identical to each other and differing from (a) only in `sharp@<0.35.0`'s bound style; (c) `tabsii-intake` alone, missing the `undici@<7.29.0` key entirely -- the #1352/#1367 shape this list exists to catch, an absence counted as a distinct value rather than a non-holder. `nanoid@<3.3.17` is identical (`>=3.3.17 <4`) across all 6 and contributes NONE of the 3 variants -- #1352's fix landed cleanly; the residual divergence is `sharp` (undeclared-intent bound-style drift, newly visible) and `undici` (#1367's known absence). Neither divergence reads as deliberate from the evidence available here (no PR, commit message or comment found explaining either), so both are recorded as drift pending reconciliation, not as declared exceptions the way `tabsii-marketplace`'s auth.ts divergence is. TIGHTENED 3 -> 2 the same day, hours after seeding, and the reason matters more than the number: the `undici` half of the residue is GONE. The jsdom 29 -> 30 bump (#1367) removed the `<8`/`<9` ceilings that were holding siblings on undici 7, and in doing so gave `tabsii-intake` the `undici@<7.29.0` key it had been missing -- so variant (c), the absence this list was built to catch, collapsed into the others and `overridesFloor` now reports `floor met` for all 6 holders. Re-measured from `origin/dev` after those merges: all six siblings carry `undici@<7.29.0`: `>=7.29.0` identically, and the ONLY remaining difference across the whole `pnpm.overrides` object is `sharp@<0.35.0` -- `^0.35.0` in `tabsii-app`/`tabsii-intake`/`tabsii-marketplace` versus `>=0.35.0` in `tabsii-crm`/`tabsii-geo`/`biffo-platform-app`, a clean 3-3 split. That divergence is LATENT, not live: sharp's newest published version is 0.35.3 and it has never published a 0.36.x, so both bounds resolve to 0.35.3 today and every lockfile in the estate agrees. It goes live the day 0.36.0 ships, because `^0.35.0` on a 0.x package means `>=0.35.0 <0.36.0` -- npm's caret locks the MINOR below 1.0.0, which is not what a reader assuming ordinary caret behaviour expects, and is the same 0.x caret trap that made `^0.2.2` unable to reach 0.3.0 elsewhere in this estate the same week. There IS already a declared answer, and it is `>=0.35.0`: BOTH canonical copies -- this repo's root `package.json` and `_skeletons/sibling-template/apps/frontend/package.json`, the source `overridesFloor` names for this very file -- carry `sharp@<0.35.0`: `>=0.35.0`. So this is not an open question needing a new decision; `tabsii-crm`/`tabsii-geo`/`biffo-platform-app` already match canonical and the three on `^0.35.0` are simply drift. Worth recording how nearly that was got wrong: reasoning from the OTHER overrides in the same object (`js-yaml@<4.3.1`: `>=4.3.1 <5`, `nanoid@<3.3.17`: `>=3.3.17 <4` -- floor plus real major ceiling, the ceiling added because #1365 saw an unbounded `>=` resolve two majors forward) suggests `>=0.35.0 <1`, which is a defensible-sounding answer arrived at WITHOUT reading the canonical copy, and would have sent six repos to a value the skeleton disagrees with. The convention argument is not wrong about `<1` being safer in the abstract; it is wrong about who gets to decide, and the fix for `sharp` is to converge the three drifted siblings on canonical, not to invent a seventh value. If `<1` is genuinely wanted, it belongs in the canonical copies FIRST and reaches the siblings from there. That reconciliation is NOT done here -- it needs a PR in each of six sibling repos and there is still no distribution channel for `pnpm.overrides` (#1352) -- so 2 is the honest live count, not the target. The target is 1, and reaching it is the remaining `sharp` half of this entry. TIGHTENED AGAIN 2 -> 1, same day, and the entry is now FULLY RECONCILED: `--check` reports `uniform across 6 repos`, meaning the whole `pnpm.overrides` object -- all six keys -- reads identically in `tabsii-app`, `tabsii-crm`, `tabsii-geo`, `tabsii-intake`, `tabsii-marketplace` and `biffo-platform-app`. The `sharp` half was closed by converging the three drifted repos on the canonical `>=0.35.0` (tabsii-app#53, tabsii-intake#70, tabsii-marketplace#76) rather than by inventing the `>=0.35.0 <1` the convention argument had suggested -- see the correction above for why that distinction mattered. Note what a baseline of 1 now means for this entry, because it is stronger than it looks: any NEW divergence in ANY override key, in any of the six repos, exceeds the baseline immediately and fails `--check` -- there is no residue left to hide inside. That is the first entry in either ratchet to reach a genuinely closed state (`mustBeUniform`'s `auth.ts` and `auth.test.ts` both sit at 2 with a declared, permanent divergence in `tabsii-marketplace`, so 1 is unreachable there by design). It also means the DISTRIBUTION half is now the only thing standing between this and a solved problem: the values agree today because they were reconciled by hand across six PRs, and nothing prevents them drifting apart again tomorrow -- #1352 remains open for exactly that reason, and the three preconditions for safe writing listed above are now one item shorter, since precondition (1), reconciling the current divergence by hand first, is DONE. SECOND ENTRY ADDED 2026-08-08: `apps/frontend/package.json` -> `engines`, seeded at 1 from a real `origin/dev` measurement AFTER the six sibling PRs landed, not predicted before them -- `--check` reports `uniform across 6 repos`. The history is the argument for tracking it: until today all six siblings declared NO `engines` at all while shipping jsdom ^30.0.1 and resolving undici 8.10.0, so every one of them was compatible-by-accident, held up only by CI pinning NODE_VERSION '22' (which resolves to 22.22.3 and happens to satisfy jsdom 30's `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0` and undici 8's `>=22.19.0`). That is the same 'fine because of a coincidence rather than a declaration' shape as #1352, one level up: not a wrong value, an ABSENT one. Six repos then had to be corrected by hand, exactly as `undici` and `sharp` were, because `package.json` is legitimately per-repo (name, version, dependencies) and so none of the file-level lists can carry it -- which is precisely the gap this list exists to cover. Seeding at 1 immediately is deliberate and is the strongest form available: with no residue, ANY future divergence -- one repo bumping its floor, one repo dropping the key -- exceeds the baseline on the next run. Note it is measured as the whole value at `engines`, not `engines.node`, so a repo adding an `npm` or `pnpm` constraint alongside `node` is caught too, with no manifest edit needed to see it. Deliberately NOT covered: `tabsii-crm`'s ROOT package.json, which is a separate install tree whose lockfile at `origin/dev` contains no jsdom and no undici entry at all -- declaring a Node floor there would assert a constraint nothing in that tree needs, and this list only measures repos holding `apps/frontend/package.json` anyway, so the root file is not a holder and never enters the count.
excludesNote: Repos removed from the measured set, with the reason stated. Read this as a DENOMINATOR CHANGE, not a tidy-up: every mode that walks the estate stops seeing these repos, so a number that improves the day one is added has not improved -- the set it was measured over got smaller. That is the exact failure scripts/protection-audit.sh was rewritten to remove (#1145), where four repos answering 404 were dropped and '27 branches checked, all protected' was a true statement about a set that silently excluded the repos least likely to be protected. So exclusion is DECLARED here rather than inferred at runtime, carries a reason, and is PRINTED on every run -- a check may shrink its scope, but it may never do so quietly. Only add a repo that genuinely cannot receive a change; 'we have not got to it yet' is drift and belongs in the count.

excludes.tabsii-lms: archived 2026-08-06 (github.com/tabsii-com/tabsii-lms) -- read-only, so it can never take a distributed file or converge on a mustBeUniform path. Its copies are frozen at whatever they were on the day it was archived. Retiring under ADR-0108; LMS is now a section of tabsii-crm.

requiresCiStepNote: The other direction of the same audit: a path a repo HOLDS, and the CI step that must therefore run over it. `supersedes` catches a repo running the wrong command; this catches a repo running no command at all. Added for #1244, where _skeletons/plugin-template/ shipped a whole terraform/ module and a ci.yml with no terraform step, so every plugin repo was scaffolded with Terraform nothing checked -- confirmed live in biffo-plugin-idea-scout (3 .tf files, zero terraform references across three workflows). The skeleton fix only ever helps repos created afterwards, and ci.yml cannot be a one-way overwrite (see supersedesNote), so the mechanism has to be an assertion here too. scripts/verify.sh cannot substitute: its terraform check is guarded by `ci_has "terraform fmt"` so a template-shipped gate never asserts over more than the repo's own CI does (the #325 trap), which means a repo whose CI checks nothing correctly gets nothing locally either -- the local half and the CI half only close the hole together. Key is a shell glob relative to the repo root; value is a fixed string that must appear on a non-comment, non-`name:` line of some workflow, so neither an explanatory comment nor a step called "Terraform fmt check" can satisfy it. Add a pair here whenever holding a class of file implies a gate; the check only fires in repos that actually hold a matching path, so a repo with no terraform/ is never reported.
supersedesNote: Raw commands each shared script replaces, checked by scripts/ci-wiring-audit.sh. shared-sync.sh gets the script INTO a repo; nothing made the repo call it, and on 2026-07-29 eleven repos merged the scripts and every one carried on running the raw command -- drift went to zero and the outcome did not move (#884). ci.yml cannot be a one-way overwrite because the path depends on that step's working-directory, so the mechanism is an assertion rather than a copy: you cannot write the line for the repo, but you can refuse to let it forget. Add a pair here whenever a shared script supersedes a command repos invoke directly; the check only fires in repos that actually hold the script, so a repo shared-sync has not reached yet is reported once, by shared-sync, rather than twice.
skeletonAdoptionNote: The fifth list, added for #1271: `<skeleton>:<path>` -> the number of applicable repos that currently hold it. `shared-sync.sh --skeleton-adoption` enumerates every path each repo skeleton owns and reports any not held by ALL of its applicable repos, then ratchets against these numbers. It exists because the estate's other detector, `--candidates`, reports a path only once >=5 repos hold it -- so the LESS adopted something was, the LESS visible it became, and the signal ran backwards against need. This list does not sample; the skeleton's own file list is known, so it enumerates. POSTURE, copied deliberately from `mustBeUniform` above and the core-upgrade orphan ratchet: pre-existing residue NEVER hard-blocks, only a REGRESSION does. A count below its baseline fails the run; a count above it is reported as improved and told to lower the baseline, because a ratchet that never tightens stops meaning anything. A NEW unadopted skeleton path with no baseline also fails -- otherwise a skeleton could gain a file nobody adopts and nothing would notice, which is the #1271 blind spot reappearing one level up. Keyed by `<skeleton>:<path>` rather than path alone because the same path legitimately differs between skeletons: `.github/workflows/codeql.yml` is 7/7 in sibling-template and 0/2 in plugin-template, and a path-only key would conflate two different facts. Measured from each repo's `origin/<base>` via `git ls-tree`, NEVER a working tree -- a stray `.venv/` in the skeleton once turned this report from 26 rows into 10,994 (#1298). NOT listed here, and deliberately: paths matching a skeleton's `.scaffold-tokens.json` are template payload that `biffo plugin create` renames (`src/example_plugin/main.py` -> `src/idea_scout/main.py`), so 0 adoption is CORRECT for them and they are reported in their own section. Deleting them would break plugin scaffolding outright. TWO CLASSIFICATIONS RECORDED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-08-04, so the baselines carry intent rather than just a number: `.github/workflows/destroy-infra.yml` (3/7 -- crm, geo, intake and marketplace lack it) and the plugin `terraform/*.tf` + `registry-schema.json` (1/2 -- biffo-plugin-ideation lacks them) are REAL GAPS to backfill, not deliberate divergence. By contrast `apps/frontend/src/lib/auth-gate.tsx` (3/7) IS deliberate -- it is where apps are meant to differ, per the mustBeUniformNote above -- and its baseline records that rather than inviting a backfill. ADDED 2026-08-05 (#1330): `services/api/tests/test_frontend_bff_paths.py` at 0/7, seeded the moment the file landed in the skeleton so the ratchet does not fire on its own arrival -- an unbaselined new path fails `--skeleton-adoption` by design (see above), and this file existing in the skeleton is enough for the enumerator to see it on the very next run, baseline or not. 0/7 is the CORRECT and EXPECTED count today, not a gap to backfill yet: this is a guard against #1330's class (a frontend calling a BFF path that does not exist -- tabsii-crm#218 and #231, the latter thirteen dead paths across three Brand HQ sections after thirteen merged milestones), and `shared-sync.sh` phase 1 runs each target's own gate before shipping, refusing the whole round if any one repo fails it. tabsii-crm#231 has merged, but the other six siblings are UNVERIFIED against this guard -- rolling it out via `filesFromSkeleton`/`files` before checking each one individually could refuse a sync round on a sibling carrying the exact defect this guard exists to catch, which is a worse failure mode than the guard not existing yet. Distribution is therefore deliberately deferred to a separate, later change: this baseline entry is bookkeeping for the ratchet only (`--skeleton-adoption` measures the skeleton's own `git ls-tree`, independent of `files`/`filesIfPresent`/`filesFromSkeleton`), and does NOT wire the file into any distribution list -- adding it to one of those would be the actual distribution act this note explicitly says is out of scope here.
